Subject: Level band precision & local-market differentials (proposal)

Team —

I uploaded the first pass of the band-refactor workbook (attached) and wanted to get alignment before we pull into the HR change window. High level asks:

- Confirm leveling definitions (IC1–5 mapping, core expectations per level).
- Agree on geo differentials: proposal includes location premia for SF/NY, London/Frankfurt (EMEA HQ markets), and a differential floor for India/SEA.
- Agree effective date (proposed: 2026-07-01) and whether we stagger by region.
- Provide 12-month cost impact for 12 planned hires and suggested mitigations if needed.

What’s in the workbook: a) canonical band midpoints & ranges b) proposed levelling language c) per-region multipliers and example role mappings.

Please review and reply with the one thing you need me to change by EOD Thu (Jun 10) so we can present to exec compensation review on Jun 15.

Attachments: 2026_comp_bands_master.xlsx (sheet: SUMMARY, LEV-MAP, GEO-PREMIUMS)

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: Re: Level band precision & local-market differentials (proposal)

Jonas —

Thanks for the workbook. Quick read-through notes (see inline + attached doc for a few specific role examples):

- Leveling: I recommend we simplify from six to five IC bands (IC1–IC5). The current mapping has overlap at the senior IC2 / junior IC3 boundary that will cause inconsistent leveling during offers.
- Midpoints: use midpoint anchoring per band and show a +/- 20% range rather than fixed min/max; this reduces edge-case offer negotiation variance.
- Geo premiums: keeps SF/NY at +18% over company baseline, EMEA HQ markets +8–10% (band-dependent), APAC lower cost regions 0–8% depending on city. I flagged London vs. continental EU as different—London should be treated explicitly.
- Benchmarking: Mercer numbers look right for 50th/75th but we should surface 25th for early-stage hires to stay competitive while managing burn.

Attachments: laura_leveling_notes.docx (examples: ML Engineer, SWE II mapping)

Subject: RE: Level band precision & local-market differentials (proposal) — Mercer Q2 summary

Hi Jonas / Laura —

Attached is the Q2 market packet you requested (Mercer_market_2026_Q2.pdf). Key takeaways we noted relevant to Redwood: 

- For cloud/infra engineering roles, 50th percentile movements across the major US markets have accelerated ~4–6% YoY; SF remains ~18% above national baseline on total cash.
- EMEA (London, DACH) lags UK premium vs. Berlin/Amsterdam by ~6–9% for senior IC levels; currency-adjusted medians are provided in the packet.
- APAC: Singapore shows mid-market convergence with APAC HQ roles; India remains >30% lower on total cash for comparable levels, though equity expectations differ.

Methodology notes: we used 2025–Q4 published data plus closed-market offers Redmond provides for peer companies. The PDF includes sample percentiles and the raw table used for your spreadsheet.

Attachment: Mercer_market_2026_Q2.pdf (methodology + percentile tables)

Best,
Ruth Kim

Jonas / team —

Thanks — high-level finance question: given the proposed midpoints and geo premia, what is the incremental run-rate for the next 12 months for the 12 hires we already budgeted? We need a headcount-true cost model (base, bonus, equity refresh assumption) to calculate runway impact and whether we need to push some hires into Q4.

Immediate asks from my side: 
- Neha, can you run the 12-hire model with both 50th and 25th offer strategies and a scenario where London premiums are applied vs. not?
- Marissa, please update recruiting plan with potential hire pacing (4/4/4 vs. 6/3/3) so we can map to cashflow.

If the incremental is >10% of monthly burn we should bring this to the CFO before exec review.

Vivek
VP Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-04T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Level band precision & local-market differentials (proposal)

Vivek —

I ran three quick scenarios and attached the CSV (cost_model_12_hires.csv). Summary (assumes hires ramp immediate H1 start and midpoints per Jonas workbook):

- Scenario A (50th baseline + full region premiums): incremental annualized OTE impact = +12.7% of current engineering payroll.
- Scenario B (25th for entry / 50th for senior): incremental = +8.9%.
- Scenario C (50th but delay 6 hires until Q4): incremental = +6.2% (spreads cash impact into next fiscal period).

Mitigation suggestions: offer more aggressive equity + cash tradeoffs for entry IC1–2 in lower-cost regions; use hiring cadence shift (Scenario C) if runway sensitivity is triggered.
